sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Trade Policy Analysis and Foreign Stakeholder Lobbying

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law, French Civil Law and Customary/Kastom Law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER-Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus), ratified by Vanuatu in 2019
Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia, New Zealand and select EU Member States
Framework Agreements with the EU under the EU-Pacific Interim Partnership Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 8 of 2014 (as amended); International Company Act [Cap. 222]; Counter-Terrorism and Transnational Organised Crime Act No. 2 of 2005 (as amended); Beneficial Ownership Act 2017 and the Beneficial Ownership Regulations (central confidential UBO register administered by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)); Companies Act [Cap. 191] (domestic); Financial Dealers Act [Cap. 70] and Financial Transactions Reporting (Enforcement) regime under the VFSC and Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport-issuing authority of the owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Vanuatu is not a Hague Apostille Convention party; documents must be notarized, authenticated by the origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the Vanuatu Embassy/Consulate or the competent consular representative)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating utility provider or licensed bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / register of directors of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate secretary of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter (past 12 months of banking conduct) for each principal/UBO
Police clearance / certificate of no criminal record for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or competent criminal records authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional CV, references, and client engagement letters evidencing the government-relations/lobbying mandate of the principals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prior employers, contracting counterparts, and instructed clients

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT sanctions list, EU CFSP asset-freeze lists, and the Vanuatu FIU domestic sanctions/advisory notices, together with domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEP), family members, and close associates under FATF standards. The government-affairs/lobbying scope (ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541820) is tiered Medium-Risk_Enhanced and requires enhanced due diligence (EDD), adverse-media checks, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, board-level sign-off of the compliance file, and ongoing transaction monitoring by the VFSC-licensed registered agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies and Trusts Registry; official portal www.vfsc.vu; name search and reservation are filed electronically through a VFSC-licensed registered agent (no direct public self-service filing API).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory names are accepted in English or French using Latin (Roman) script only; Bislama is not a statutory naming language. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into an English or French Roman-script equivalent at reservation, and the registered name must contain the suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. The Registrar rejects names with characters outside the standard Latin alphabet, confusing similarity to an existing entity, or names misleading as to activity, scale, or sponsorship.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant (acting through its VFSC-licensed registered agent) may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, attaching a fresh official name-search certificate and at least two alternative names; the Registrar must respond within five business days. Where rejection is based on public-interest, misleading, or statutorily protected grounds, the applicant may appeal to the Minister of Trade and Commerce, and thereafter to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222]. In parallel, the agent may submit a new reservation request with alternative names to avoid delay; a successful reservation may be extended once by the Registrar upon payment of the applicable extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as a substitute for the statutory registered office. Every International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Vanuatu at the premises of its licensed registered agent, where statutory records and the UBO register reside. Remote and virtual working is acceptable for the conduct of the lobbying-advisory business abroad, but the legal seat and registered address are the agent's physical office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered agent premises: Medium (estimated 5-10% annual probability of VFSC or FIU compliance inspection covering the agent's client files); company's own Vanuatu premises: Low (less than 5% per annum) given the tax-exempt offshore IC structure with no local employees, although the Medium-Risk_Enhanced government-lobbying scope may trigger targeted FIU review upon adverse-media or sanctions events.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act, Cap. 222 (Vanuatu), as amended; Part II (Incorporation of International Companies), sections 5-11; Part IV (Shares and Debentures), sections 24-31; Part V (Registered Office), sections 34-36; Part VI (Directors and Officers), sections 37-45; Part VII (Meetings and Resolutions), sections 49-55.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry Division, Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: International Company Incorporation Application (Form IC-1), submitted with Memorandum and Articles of Association to the VFSC Registrar of International Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the International Companies Act, Cap. 222. The authorised capital may be stated in any currency. No escrow account or capital deposit is required for incorporation; share capital can be issued as fully or partly paid as determined by the first board of directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association be and are hereby appointed as the first directors of the Company pursuant to section 37 of the International Companies Act, Cap. 222 and shall hold office until the first annual general meeting. 2. The registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu, as specified in the registered agent consent. 3. The allotment of one ordinary share at par value to the first subscriber/shareholder be approved and recorded in the register of members. 4. The directors be and are hereby authorized to execute banking mandates, engage the licensed registered agent, and file all required declarations with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission. 5. This resolution takes effect immediately and the chairperson is directed to execute all documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Registered Agent and Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint and execute the registered agent agreement with a VFSC-licensed registered agent in Vanuatu. Instruct the agent to submit three ranked proposed company names via the VFSC online portal or in person at the VFSC counter. Names must include 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or the abbreviation 'Ltd', 'Corp', or 'Inc'. Submit a name reservation request with certified identification of the proposed shareholder(s). After approval of name availability, the reservation is held for 30 days. Payment of the name reservation fee is made to the VFSC cashier. Receive the name reservation certificate from the registry.
required_dossiers: Original or certified copy of passport or national ID of each subscriber/shareholder
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
Certificate of Incorporation or registration document of corporate shareholder (if applicable)
Licensed registered agent engagement letter
Name reservation application with three proposed names
Remittance of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused as undesirable or confusingly similar, file a fresh name reservation application with alternative names. If the reservation expires, reapply and pay the fee again. If the agent's engagement is queried, confirm the agent's VFSC licence number and submit a renewed consent letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Vanuatu-licensed registered agent or legal counsel to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English. The Memorandum must state the company name, registered office address, authorised share capital, and the number/type of shares. The Articles must adopt Table A of the International Companies Act where applicable and include permitted objects; for a government affairs and lobbying consultancy, state the principal business as 'cross-border trade policy analysis, foreign stakeholder lobbying, and public affairs advisory services' and include an express prohibition on domestic retail business in Vanuatu. Execute the Memorandum and Articles by each subscriber, with signatures witnessed. Deliver the executed documents to the registered agent for lodging.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Application (Form IC-1) signed by the registered agent
Memorandum and Articles of Association duly subscribed and witnessed
Consent of first director(s) to act (Form IC-4 or equivalent)
Consent of the registered agent to act as registered office provider
Name reservation certificate
Certified identification documents of all subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC queries inconsistent clauses between the Memorandum and Articles, file amended constitutive documents via the registered agent. If the stated objects are deemed too broad relative to ISIC 7020, narrow the object clause to specifically cover advisory and lobbying services and refile. If execution attestation is defective, re-execute before a notary public or a witness qualified under the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Registration Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry Division, Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed registered agent files the complete incorporation package with the VFSC Registry either electronically via the VFSC portal or physically at the registry counter. The application must include the name reservation certificate, executed memorandum/articles, director and registered agent consents, and the signed Form IC-1. Pay the official state filing fee of USD 350 (or equivalent in Vatu) via bank transfer or card at the VFSC cashier. The registrar checks for compliance with the International Companies Act, Cap. 222 and issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the company registration number and date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association (two certified copies)
Form IC-1 signed by the registered agent
Consent to act of each director/officer (Form IC-4)
Receipt or proof of fee payment
Copy of the registered agent licence and consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC rejects the application for incomplete dossiers, resubmit the missing consents or certified copies within the VFSC's specified cure period. If the registered agent fails authentication, re-submit the Form IC-1 with a correct authorised signatory. If there is a defect in the name or object clause, amend and refile. The certificate, once issued, is conclusive evidence of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of First Directors and Officers; Execution of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; minutes kept at the registered office under International Companies Act, Cap. 222
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, the subscriber(s) act as sole incorporator(s) and appoint the first director(s) in writing or by unanimous resolution. The first director(s) hold a statutory board meeting (physically or by written resolution) to adopt the first board resolution approving share subscription, adoption of the registered office at the agent's address, appointment of a company secretary (if not exempt), and opening of banking signatory authorities. Record the minutes in the minute book and have all directors sign. File a copy of the resolution and register of directors with the VFSC if required; maintain originals at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Register of Directors and Officers (Form IC-5 if applicable)
Register of Members and Share Allotment sheet
First board resolution (signed minutes)
Consent to act of each director/officer
Registered office consent confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If directors' consent forms are challenged, obtain fresh signatures and notarise if required. If the VFSC requires secondary filing of the director register, submit within 14 days of appointment. If a director is disqualified under section 45 of the Act, replace immediately and file an amended consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Ministry of Finance for Tax Identification and Exempt Status Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM) - Tax and Customs Division; Department of Customs and Inland Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Certificate of Incorporation and memorandum/articles to the MFEM Tax and Customs Division to obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and confirm the International Company's exemption from income tax, VAT, and withholding tax under the International Companies Act and the Value Added Tax Act. Complete the registration for the 'tax-exempt zone' classification and obtain an official exempt status letter. If the company will conduct economic activities in Vanuatu requiring a business licence, separate local council licensing may apply, but an IC engaged strictly in foreign lobbying/advisory may obtain a certificate of non-resident business status.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified copy)
First board resolution appointing directors and officers
Registered agent confirmation letter
VAT registration form (if applicable)
TIN application form (Form TR-001 or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry queries the exempt status, submit a legal opinion referencing sections 8 and 9 of the International Companies Act confirming the IC's income tax exemption. If VAT registration is erroneously imposed for foreign-only services, provide a written declaration that all services are rendered to non-residents and no imports/exports of goods occur in Vanuatu. If the TIN is delayed, escalate to the TIN helpdesk with proof of filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - Licensing and Superannuation Division; for business licence matters, the Vanuatu Department of Industry and the Provincial/Municipal Council Business Licence Office in Port Vila
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Company Tax Exempt Status Certificate and Business Licence (Foreign Enterprises Licence) under the Business Licence Act (Cap. 88)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC) under the Environmental Protection and Conservation Act, No. 12 of 2003
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt - Administrative and advisory office-based services under ISIC 7020 are categorised as low-impact 'non-prescribed activities'; no full EIA report required unless physical office premises involve significant construction or waste generation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For a government affairs/lobbying office: zero industrial wastewater discharge; domestic sanitary effluent to municipal sewer per Port Vila urban sewerage regulations; compliance with Vanuatu's ambient air quality standards for any standby generator (VOCs and NOx limits under the National Air Quality Policy); proper segregation and disposal of electronic waste (e-waste) via licensed recyclers; adherence to solid waste management permits if the office produces hazardous materials such as printer toners or batteries

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services (VFES) confirming occupancy load, fire extinguishers, and evacuation plan; structural load inspection certificate from the Public Works Department for the leased office premises (where applicable); workplace clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Cap. 180) covering first aid kit, sanitation, and electrical safety inspection; business clearance letter from the Port Vila Municipal Council (if operating from a commercial lease) verifying compliance with zoning, signage, and public liability insurance

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Commission (VCIR), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, Port Vila; corporate/offshore-sector regulator and company registry: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC); primary revenue portal: https://customsinlandrevenue.gov.vu (VAT registration and filing); corporate registry portal: https://www.vfsc.vu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] holds no domestic income-tax registration and is not issued a TIN because Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax and the IC is a statutory Tax_Exempt_Zone entity (exemption at s.112, IC Act [Cap. 222]). SOP: (1) obtain the IC certificate of incorporation and 'International Company' status from VFSC through a licensed registered agent; (2) use the VFSC company/registration number as the statutory identifier for all banking, contracting and KYC purposes; (3) VAT registration with VCIR is required only if the entity makes taxable supplies within Vanuatu — which an IC is statutorily prohibited from doing (no business with Vanuatu residents, no local landholding); consequently no VAT ID is procured for a pure offshore government-affairs advisory/lobbying operation; (4) should anomalous local revenue activity arise, file VCIR VAT registration Form 1 within 14 days of crossing the registration threshold and obtain a VAT number; (5) no customs, business-licence or social-security registrations apply to an offshore-only IC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the IC is exempt from all present and future Vanuatu taxes, duties, levies and imposts on income, profits, capital gains, distributions and branch results (IC Act [Cap. 222], s.112); the exemption is worldwide in scope but contingent on refraining from domestic Vanuatu-resident business; ICs are also outside the scope of the turnover-based VAT given the prohibition on local taxable supplies, preserving the IC as an offshore tax-exempt platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vanuatu has no income tax law; therefore no check-the-box, fiscal-transparent, or hybrid-mismatch elections exist for ICs, and entity-level tax exemption is automatic and non-elective. Available elections of consequence: (1) voluntary VAT registration under the VAT Act for a person below the compulsory turnover threshold (practically unavailable to an IC because of the prohibition on local taxable supplies); (2) election to convert the IC into a domestic company under the Companies Act [Cap. 191] — a one-way decision that terminates tax-exempt status and subjects the business to future local tax, VAT registration and business-licence obligations; (3) no CFC, thin-capitalisation, or transfer-pricing elections apply because no income tax or withholding tax is levied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — imposed by the Value Added Tax Act No. 12 of 1998 (as amended) and administered by VCIR on the destination principle; supplemented by customs duties under the Customs Act [Cap. 248] on imports; no separate GST, sales tax or turnover tax exists. ICs and their offshore supplies are outside the domestic VAT charge; exports of goods and exported services are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VUV 4,000,000 (approx. USD 34,000) of taxable turnover in any 12-month period for compulsory registration (VAT Act s.6); threshold and rate are fixed by national law and confirmed annually in the Appropriation Act — verify the prevailing figure with VCIR at onboarding; supplies made by a non-resident to Vanuatu recipients do not by themselves trigger registration unless the non-resident maintains a local fixed establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, digital stamping or clearance e-invoicing regime applies in Vanuatu. VCIR accepts paper and PDF tax invoices. Registered persons must issue full tax invoices for taxable supplies (simplified/receipt invoices permitted for transactions under VUV 5,000), retain sufficient transactional records for audit, and file VAT returns on a monthly basis. A national digitalisation programme (ASYCUDA World) is being phased in for customs declarations, but there is currently no machine-readable continuous transaction-control obligation for services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for: (i) exports of goods that physically leave Vanuatu; and (ii) 'exported services' — services supplied to a person who is outside Vanuatu at the time of supply, the benefit of which is enjoyed wholly outside Vanuatu, including international consulting, cross-border trade-policy analysis, and foreign-stakeholder lobbying or advocacy services for non-resident principals. For the ISIC 7020 Government_Affairs_Lobbying entity, the standard criteria are: the principal is a non-resident foreign stakeholder; the engagement letter specifies offshore performance and foreign-law advisory; the invoice is addressed abroad in foreign currency; performance occurs and benefits are enjoyed outside Vanuatu; and no advocacy or related benefit is delivered in Vanuatu. Because an IC is statutorily exempt from all Vanuatu taxes and is barred from domestic business, it does not register for VAT; its offshore supplies are outside the VAT net, so there is no VAT to zero-rate and no refundable input VAT to claim. A domestic (non-IC) advisory entity would become VAT-registered only on crossing the VUV 4,000,000 threshold and would then zero-rate qualifying service exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic goods declaration) — for any goods movements
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / freight receipt evidencing physical export from Vanuatu
Commercial invoice and underlying export or lobbying-services contract naming the non-resident principal
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/credit advice evidencing foreign-currency receipt of the export consideration
Recipient non-residency evidence (foreign incorporation certificate, foreign tax ID, or overseas address/official ID) substantiating offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VCIR may audit zero-rated claims post-export and retrospectively claw back wrongly zero-rated output VAT with interest. VAT evasion and false-declaration offences (VAT Act s.76) carry a fine of up to VUV 10,000,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 2 years; the Commissioner may additionally impose shortfall penalties and interest, and adjust input credits within the statutory assessment window. Vanuatu maintains no exchange controls and imposes no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure in this dossier reflects prevailing banking/AML best practice for documenting inward remittances rather than a statutory clawback trigger. Fraudulent zero-rating documentation may concurrently expose the IC to VFSC deregistration, disqualification of its registered agent, and reporting or sanctions under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2014.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) – the statutory monetary authority and foreign exchange administrator under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act [Cap 125] and the International Companies Act [Cap 222].
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu Vatu (VUV) is freely convertible on both current and capital account operations for International Companies. Vanuatu maintains no exchange control legislation. Profit remittance, dividend repatriation, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred offshore to non-resident shareholders without prior central bank approval. The practical hurdle is not regulatory restriction but correspondent banking due diligence and clearing-house reputation risk.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu imposes no mandatory surrender timeline or conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in any convertible foreign currency or repatriated to the International Company's settlement account with any licensed bank in Vanuatu. For an ISIC 7020 lobbying advisory entity, cross-border service fees and retainer payments are classified as service exports and are entirely exempt from surrender and conversion requirements. The only compliance obligation is statistical reporting under the RBV's Balance of Payments regulations for transactions exceeding VUV 5,000,000 per calendar year.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for regulated offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed in reputable fintech jurisdictions (e.g., United Kingdom FCA, Lithuania, Gibraltar, or Singapore) to support multi-currency treasury operations. Legal constraint: an offshore EMI has no direct clearing access to the RBV's local settlement systems; any VUV-denominated disbursement must ultimately route through a licensed Vanuatu commercial bank. Vanuatu currently has no domestic EMI licensing class, so the IC may engage an offshore EMI as a payment agent, provided the EMI's KYC and AML framework is at least equivalent to FATF standards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical director attendance is not statutorily mandated under Vanuatu law. However, due to the Medium-Risk Enhanced classification of the ISIC 7020 government-affairs lobbying sector, tier-1 banks typically require at least one substantive director or ultimate beneficial owner to complete an in-person KYC interview at the Port Vila branch. Where all directors are non-resident, banks permit a video teleconference interview with a notarized remote interview certificate and a certified KYC pack. Pure remote account opening without any interview is available only after a full compliance-committee review and a VFSC corporate registry cross-check.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status of lobbying principals or client legal beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited entity accounts for the preceding two years, executed client engagement contracts, a certified extract from the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) corporate registry, and an independent PEP screening certificate from a recognized provider showing no adverse matches or confirmations of legitimate non-executive advisory roles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk cross-border wire patterns to or from opaque jurisdictions or secrecy-haven territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A source-of-wealth declaration signed by the beneficial owner, 12 months of original bank statements showing origin of funds, a board resolution approving each recurring wire with commercial rationale, and a treasury narrative memorandum demonstrating that the cross-border pattern is ordinary for government-relations retainer business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership structure utilizing nominee shareholders or offshore trusts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deed or nominee shareholder agreement, individual identification of settlors and all identifiable beneficiaries, an organizational ownership chart from the IC through to natural persons, and a certificate of current incumbency issued by the registered agent in Vanuatu evidencing economic substance and compliance with the International Companies Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 priority wire transfers. The acquiring Vanuatu bank mandates the inclusion of the IC's VFSC registration number and the purpose code 'EQUI' for share capital or 'LOAN' for shareholder subordinated debt. Inward remittance vouchers must carry the phrase 'International Company – Non-Resident Account' to preserve tax-exempt status. Verification comprises the bank's automated AML screening, a VU beneficiary ownership declaration form, and a real-time check against the RBV financial intelligence unit sanctions list. No central bank approval is required for capital infusion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound retainer and advisory disbursements is SWIFT MT103 with SWIFT gpi (Global Payments Innovation) tracking for real-time confirmation. For large international policy-research procurement contracts, a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 may be issued through ANZ Vanuatu or BSP Vanuatu, with confirmation by a top-tier correspondent bank (e.g., Citi, HSBC, or Standard Chartered). Domestic disbursements inside Vanuatu settle via the local Vanuatu Automated Transfer System (VATS), which clears VUV in T+0. CHIPS and Fedwire are permitted downstream rails for USD settlement through correspondent banks, but the primary instruction must carry the IC's legal entity identifier and a compliant purpose code for advisory services.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanuatu Vatu deliverable currency forwards via RBV-licensed authorized dealers
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for VUV/USD and VUV/AUD where physical delivery is impractical
Cross-currency swaps between VUV and USD, AUD, and EUR executed through a licensed commercial bank
Vanilla FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) with tenors up to 12 months for operating cash-flow hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of an International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 calendar months after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; anniversary-based, not fixed to the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty accrues per the VFSC prescribed fee schedule on a monthly basis; persistent default for two or more consecutive anniversaries triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222], resulting in loss of legal personality, freezing of assets held in the corporate name, and inability of directors to transact on behalf of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Vanuatu registered agent maintaining the registered office on behalf of the company and filing the corresponding confirmation with the VFSC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary of incorporation, coincident with the payment of the VFSC annual government fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment of the registered agent's renewal invoice results in resignation of the agent and cancellation of the registered office; the company is then unable to file its annual return or be lawfully transacted, leading to administrative strike-off by the VFSC and potential director disqualification under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222]

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit applies to a standard exempt Vanuatu International Company; compulsory audit arises only where the IC holds a VFSC financial-services licence (for example banking, insurance, or securities dealing) or where the board of directors voluntary resolves to appoint an auditor; there is no revenue, asset, or shareholding threshold that imposes an audit for the exempt IC structure
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework is prescribed for tax-exempt International Companies under Vanuatu law; where financial statements are prepared for management or financing purposes, IFRS or a simplified internal basis consistent with the company's transaction trail is customarily used; the VFSC AML/CFT Code separately requires maintenance of adequate records that accurately explain all transactions and enable reconstruction of the company's financial position

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vanuatu maintains no public register of beneficial owners and imposes no statutory annual UBO confirmation filing; the registered agent must nevertheless perform an annual 'know your client' risk review under the VFSC AML/CFT Code, and any transfer of shares must first be recorded in the company's Register of Members before the next anniversary annual return is submitted; beneficial-ownership particulars are collected and retained confidentially by the registered agent for production to law-enforcement and the VFSC upon lawful demand
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders), including transfer entries
Register of Secretaries (where a corporate secretary is appointed)
Minute Book (resolutions of shareholders and directors)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per year, being the prevailing market range for a licensed Vanuatu registered agent inclusive of the registered office address, annual return preparation, and basic compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for an exempt International Company without a VFSC licence; where a voluntary independent review or audit is commissioned, the prevailing market range is USD 3,000 - 7,000 for an advisory entity of comparable size

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties. International Companies are treated as tax-exempt within the jurisdiction. VAT registration is required only if taxable supplies exceed VUV 10,000,000 per annum. The only periodic charges are the VFSC annual renewal fee and Government services levy.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Not applicable – no corporate income tax return exists in Vanuatu. The sole annual compliance filing is the VFSC Annual Return / Renewal Declaration filed electronically by the registered agent through the VFSC online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual renewal is due on or before each anniversary of incorporation. A VAT return is required quarterly, due within 30 days after the end of each quarter, if the IC exceeds the VAT registration threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Company Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and VFSC registration certificate number of the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners are not named on this box; the registered agent attests to corporate details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Business Address and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residential or business street address, postal address, and name of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent address must be within Vanuatu; a non-resident principal may remain undisclosed to the public registry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Authorised Share Capital and Shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of issued share capital, par value, and class of shares, with names of registered shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; beneficial owners must be disclosed only to the registered agent for AML/CFT records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationality, and date of appointment of each director and secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors may be used if licensed and properly appointed; the agent must hold proof of consent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Tax and Economic Substance Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the company is not engaged in a Vanuatu taxable activity or a relevant ESR activity without substance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs with no local physical presence must affirm that core income-generating activities occur outside Vanuatu.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late renewal attracts a monthly surcharge equal to 10% of the unpaid annual fee; failure to file for six consecutive months leads to automatic strike-off, forfeiture of assets to the Registrar, and reinstatement only upon payment of all arrears and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu imposes no withholding tax on distributions, so no domestic treaty relief procedure is needed. Where a foreign tax credit requires proof of non-taxation, an IC may obtain a certificate of tax residence or non-assessment from the Vanuatu Department of Finance and Economic Management; however, Vanuatu has no comprehensive double taxation agreements in force. Only tax information exchange agreements exist. The non-resident shareholder seeking treaty benefits must make a claim in their residence jurisdiction and provide a Vanuatu tax status certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT 0% on cross-border royalties and interest; treaty rate N/A due to absence of DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No local transfer pricing documentation threshold exists under Vanuatu law, and no Local File or Master File is required. For multinational groups, the common reporting threshold of EUR 750 million consolidated group revenue applies only under foreign CbC rules; Vanuatu does not mandate or exchange CbC reports.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu International Companies are subject to the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019. ESR applies to relevant activities: banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, holding company, intellectual property holding, and distribution/service centres. Government affairs lobbying and management consultancy (ISIC 7020) is not itself a listed relevant activity; however, an IC that also operates as a distribution and service centre or IP holding vehicle must satisfy the full economic substance test, including being directed and managed in Vanuatu, maintaining physical premises in Vanuatu, having adequate staff and expenditure in Vanuatu, and performing core income-generating activities in Vanuatu.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Vanuatu IC that lacks economic substance to invoice cross-border lobbying services from a shell mailbox, while actual management, staff, and decision-making occur in a high-tax jurisdiction, with the purpose of avoiding foreign corporate income taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign revenue authorities may recharacterise the IC as a sham and impose underpayment penalties of 100% to 200% of the tax avoided, plus interest. In Vanuatu, a false declaration to the VFSC may trigger a fine of up to VUV 1,000,000 and deregistration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and shadow directors who knowingly enable the sham can be held personally liable in the foreign jurisdiction for unpaid corporate taxes, subjected to civil asset freezing, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in an ESR relevant activity such as distribution and service centre or IP holding without an actual physical office, resident directors, employees, or core income-generating activity in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VFSC may levy a financial penalty of up to VUV 1,000,000, order rectification, or strike the company off the register; repeat violations may attract criminal prosecution and higher fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to ensure compliance with the ESR may be personally fined, disqualified from managing any Vanuatu company for up to five years, and face imprisonment of up to two years if contempt is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving retainer fees from parties seeking to lobby foreign government officials, while failing to conduct beneficial ownership due diligence, ignoring politically exposed person status, or facilitating a corrupt payment program disguised as advisory fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Vanuatu AML/CFT laws, a company may face civil penalties up to VUV 10,000,000, revocation of its registered agent or financial license, freezing of bank accounts, and forfeiture of illegal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be subject to personal fines of up to VUV 25,000,000 and imprisonment up to 15 years for money laundering, bribery conspiracy, or wilful blindness to corruption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false VFSC annual declaration stating the company is dormant or is not subject to economic substance, while the foreign beneficial owner actually carries on lobbying activity through undisclosed arrangements or unlicensed nominee directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Companies Act imposes fines of up to VUV 1,000,000 per false declaration and permits the Registrar to cancel the company's registration, effectively dissolving it and preventing the company from enforcing contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signatories of false statutory declarations accept personal criminal liability and can be barred from serving as directors in Vanuatu for a cumulative period of five years; foreign courts may pierce the corporate veil and render the foreign principal and nominal directors jointly and severally liable.
